content: Cap Blanc rock shelter is an archaeological site located in France. It is a rock shelter that was occupied by prehistoric human populations during the Upper Paleolithic period, around 15,000 to 13,000 years ago. Excavations at the site have uncovered stone tools, animal bones, and other artifacts that provide insights into the lifeways of the hunter-gatherer groups that lived there. The site is considered an important example of a Magdalenian culture rock shelter from the Late Pleistocene era in Europe. However, I don't have detailed information about the specific archaeological findings or the full history and significance of this particular rock shelter site. My knowledge about Cap Blanc is relatively limited.
